statement.p: Part of the surface x=z^3, where 0\le x,y\le {5}^{-\frac32};\quad f(x,y,z)=x

static.solution:
z=g( x,y )= x^{1/3} and use the formula for the surface integral over a graph: \iint_S f( x,y,z ) \,dS=\iint_{\mathcal{D}} f\left(x,y,g( x,y )\right)\sqrt{1+ g_x^2+ g_y^2} \,dx \,dy\ \quad \mathbf{(1)} where \mathcal{D} is the square \left[0,{5}^{-\frac32}\right]\times \left[0,{5}^{-\frac32}\right] in the xy-plane. We compute the integrand in \mathbf{(1)}: g_x = \frac13 x^{-2/3},\quad g_y = 0 \Downarrow \sqrt{1+g_x^2+g_y^2}=\sqrt{1+\frac19 x^{-4/3}} f\left(x,y,g(x,y)\right) = x Substituting in \mathbf{(1)} we get: \iint_S f( x,y,z ) \,dS= \int_0^{{5}^{-\frac32}} \int_0^{{5}^{-\frac32}} x\sqrt{1+\frac19 x^{-4/3}} \,dx \,dy={5}^{-\frac32} \int_0^{{5}^{-\frac32}} x\sqrt{1+\frac19 x^{-4/3}} \,dx We compute the integral using the substitution \frac13 x^{-2/3}= \tan \theta. Then: \sqrt{1+\frac19 x^{-4/3}} = \sqrt{1+{\tan}^2 \theta }=\frac{1}{\cos \theta } -\frac29 x^{-5/3} \,dx = \frac{1}{\cos^2\theta } \,d\theta \Downarrow x \,dx=-\frac92\cdot \frac{1}{\cos^2\theta } x^{8/3} \,d\theta =-\frac{1}{18} \frac{\cos^2\theta }{\sin^4\theta }d\theta Hence: \sqrt{1+\frac19 x^{-4/3}}\cdot x \,dx=-\frac{1}{18} \frac{\cos \theta }{\sin^4\theta } \,d\theta We obtain the following integral, which we compute by substituting u= \sin \theta, \,du= \cos \theta \,d\theta :
With a=3\text{,} \quad b=5\text{,} \quad c=\sqrt{34} \quad \text{and } \alpha={\tan}^{-1} \left(\frac{5}3\right)
\iint_S f( x,y,z ) \,dS= {5}^{-\frac32} \int_{\pi/2}^{{\tan}^{-1} \left(\frac{5}3\right)} -\frac{1}{18} \frac{\cos \theta }{\sin^4\theta } \,d\theta=-\frac{{5}^{-\frac32}}{18}\int_1^{\sin \left({\tan}^{-1} \left(\frac{5}3\right)\right)=\frac{5}{\sqrt{34}}} \frac{1}{ u^4} \,du= \frac{{5}^{-\frac32}}{54}\cdot \frac{1}{u^3}\bigg|_1^{\frac{5}{\sqrt{34}}}= \frac{{5}^{-\frac32}}{54}\left(\frac{34\sqrt{34}}{125}-1\right) \approx 0.00097065
